PullRequest.Title: chat: add link context menu actions
PullRequest.Body:
chat: add link context menu actions

Add link-specific actions to the chat transcript context menu.

- Add Copy Link for rendered response links and preserve the semantic link target.
- Add Open With for file-system resources with registered editors.
- Pass typed link context through ChatContext without changing existing action behavior.
- Extend tests and component fixture services for link menu behavior.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct and render a chat transcript widget
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Widget dependency injection and constructor setup must complete before the transcript is usable. The newly injected file and editor-resolver services add only references; the editor resolver is already registered as an eager workbench singleton, so no new lazy initialization is pulled onto this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chat list widgets, normally one per visible chat host; added work is two service references per widget.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One constructor invocation per chat list widget; no queue, IPC, or fan-out was added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The editor resolver's existing registration/cache state is unchanged; widget construction neither populates nor invalidates it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed constructor parameters and eager resolver registration were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously hosted chat widgets varies, but the changed constructor work is constant per widget and does not instantiate a newly lazy heavyweight service.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no new startup/render boundary or heavyweight eager allocation is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the transcript context menu on a normal, HTTP, or file-backed link
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contextmenu handler synchronously finds the nearest anchor, parses one target, and for a provider-backed non-HTTP resource computes matching registered editors before showing the menu. HTTP(S) targets short-circuit before provider/editor lookup.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One clicked link and the workbench's registered editor patterns; cost does not scale with transcript length or number of rendered links.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the UI event loop, exactly once per explicit context-menu event; no background tasks or aggregate fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: File-provider presence is an in-memory scheme-map lookup. Editor registrations and flattened state use the resolver's existing invalidation lifecycle; matching is recomputed for the one resource without filesystem, network, extension-host IPC, or transcript-wide scanning.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the handler, file-service lookup, and editor-resolver implementation show one in-process lookup over registered editors and no expensive boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Custom editor registration counts vary, so the exact synchronous matching cost is uncertain, but realistic cardinality is bounded by registered editor patterns and the trigger is an explicit context-menu invocation rather than rendering, scrolling, or input.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added synchronous work is bounded, user-triggered, and in-memory, with no evidence of perceptible menu latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Copy Link from a rendered chat response
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action awaits one system clipboard write, then emits an accessibility status. The clipboard write is the action's required critical-path operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the semantic link target to the system clipboard; desktop delegates once to the native host, while web performs one browser clipboard API call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one clipboard call per Copy Link invocation, independent of transcript or link count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Rendered response links had no Copy Link command in this transcript menu; attachment-resource copying continued to use its existing single writeResources call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action awaits completion before announcing that the link was copied.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Length of one selected link target and user invocation frequency; no collection fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One write per user command invocation; rapid independent invocations are not coalesced, matching ordinary clipboard command semantics.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is appropriate for mutable system clipboard state; the command copies only the selected target.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed action directly awaits writeText once, and desktop/web implementations were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Platform clipboard latency varies, but payload size is one link target and boundary cardinality is fixed at one.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the single required clipboard boundary is the explicit feature operation and is neither repeated nor amplified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Open With for a provider-backed file link
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action calls editorService.openEditor for one resource with PICK. Resolver work creates the editor picker; after a user selection, normal editor creation/opening must complete for the resource.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Conditionally wait for installed extension registrations when the resource matches the resolver's startup cache before presenting/resolving editor choices.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero after extension registration completes; otherwise at most one existing registration barrier for the single resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This transcript-menu route did not invoke Open With; the same resolver barrier already applied whenever the resource was opened with EditorResolution.PICK elsewhere.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can delay picker resolution only during the existing cold-start registration window.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: After the user selects an editor, that editor may resolve/read the one chosen file through its existing file-system provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one resource open per action invocation; no operation is issued for every available editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The transcript context menu lacked this route; opening the same link or using Open With elsewhere performed the same single-resource editor/file work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Any selected editor's ordinary resource-open work is required to display that file and occurs after the picker choice.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected file resource and the bounded set of registered editor choices; no transcript-wide or per-choice boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One resolver/open request per command invocation. The picker serializes user selection; no per-editor opens or concurrent file operations are launched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Available editors come from the resolver's existing registration state; extension-registration cache is cleared once registrations complete. File/model caching is owned by the selected editor and unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the one-resource resolver path and conditional extension-registration barrier; downstream file cost is editor-dependent but not multiplied by the change.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The selected editor and provider determine actual open latency, but cardinality remains one resource and one user-selected editor.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new action performs the necessary single-resource Open With workflow without extra fan-out or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke existing chat context-menu commands after typed link context wrapping
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing commands unwrap the action context with an object/type check before performing their prior behavior.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One context object per command invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged command-level execution; no scheduling, queue, or coalescing changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache interaction was added; widget/session lookups retain their prior behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed unwrapping call sites are visible in the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the added work is a constant-time guard and property read per command invocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: typed context propagation adds only constant-time checks and does not increase existing boundary cardinality.
